post.summary: Generate an image or a video
post.description: Starts a generation and answers 202 with the pending creation; the brand's base style, cast look, and reference photos are applied server-side. An image debits its model's price in credits. With `mediaType` set to `video` the image is generated and then animated into a clip of the same `aspectRatio` with the brand's video model, both paid up front, and the creation returned is the clip. Prices are in the brand's `models` list. Poll the single-creation endpoint (ideally with `wait`) until `status` is `complete`. Send an `Idempotency-Key` header to make retries safe: a replay returns the original creation instead of debiting again.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Any unique string up to 200 characters. A retry with the same key and body replays the first response instead of running again, for 24 hours. The same key with a different body is a `409`, as is a retry while the first request is still running (with `Retry-After`).

post.description: A `manual` series runs a fixed recipe and requires `theme`, `format` (post, carousel, story, or reel), and `cadenceDays`. An `autopilot` series requires a `goal` (with optional `guidance`, `formats`, `maxPerWeek`, `postsPerWeek`, `weekdaysUtc`, `hourPinned`, and `creditBudgetMonthly`) and plans its own content from measured results. A reel is a short 9:16 video animated from a generated still; `audioMode` and `soundIds` decide its sound and `videoModel` overrides the brand's default. `socialAccountId` names the connected Instagram or TikTok account to publish to; an empty string stops items at ready. `delivery` decides who makes the post: `auto` posts it, `handoff` gives it to the operator (a draft in TikTok's inbox, or a Discord message with the file, caption, and sound for Instagram) and the slot waits as `handedOff` until the post appears on the account. TikTok's API attaches no sound and has no stories, so a TikTok series defaults to `handoff`, mixes in uploaded sounds only, and on autopilot plans reels only; `auto` on TikTok needs the `tiktok` settings and TikTok's approval of the app. `crosspostAccountIds` also sends every slot to other connected accounts. Without `publishWrite` the new series starts paused, since an active series posts on its own.

post.summary: Add a post to a series
post.description: Adds one slot on top of what the series plans, on autopilot as much as on a manual series; the scheduler never drops it. Give it at most one media source: `creationId` (a finished image, or a clip from the animate endpoint for a reel), `assetId` (a photo, or a kind `video` asset, which makes the slot a reel, or a story when `format` is `story`), `sourceUrl` (a public image or video URL, imported like `POST /v1/assets`), or `assetIds` (2 to 10 photo assets, in order, posted as a carousel of the operator's own slides). A supplied photo is cropped to the slot's shape, analyzed so the autopilot knows what it shows, captioned on an autopilot series, and the slot answers `ready`; a supplied video is rendered to the 9:16 spec with the series' overlay and a sound (`soundId`, or the series' first allowed sound) after the response, so the slot answers `generating` and turns `ready` on `GET /v1/series/{id}` once rendered (or `failed` with the reason). A story video runs up to 60 seconds and publishes without a caption or an Instagram sound. Without media the slot is planned around `idea` (or invents one); `generateNow` generates its images inline, one credit each; a reel slot generates a still, reviews it, then animates it. Omit `scheduledFor` for the series' next free posting hour. A not-yet-generated planned slot at the same time is taken over.
